deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is folio 24 of Riemann's student essay 'Versuch einer allgemeinen Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation' (dated 1847, first printed in the Gesammelte Werke, 1876). The red marginalia are an editor's instructions for the printed text. They convert Riemann's notation ^x∂^ν_z into ∂_x^ν z, ask that the footnote be set 'Als Note unter den Text', and mark 'a linea' (new line).

The page closes the argument of the previous page. There, for negative order μ, the value (1/Π(-μ-1)) ∫_k^x (x-t)^{-μ-1} z(t) dt was shown to be a value of ∂_x^μ z. Changing the lower limit k to k1 adds
(1/Π(-μ-1)) ∫_{k1}^{k} (x-t)^{-μ-1} z(t) dt = Σ_{n≥0} x^{-μ-1-n}/Π(-μ-1-n) · ∫_{k1}^{k} (-t)^n/n! z(t) dt.
This is obtained by binomial expansion of (x-t)^{-μ-1}. The integrals are constants in x.

Riemann's conclusion on this page:
(a) The procedure always leads to the same 'system of values'. He therefore restricts the concept of the derivative to that system. This reduces its determination to known quantities, from which the properties of ∂^ν and its values for particular functions can be derived.

(b) Definition for ν < 0, with z continuous between k and x (Π(s) = Γ(s+1)):
∂_x^ν z = (1/Γ(-ν)) ∫_k^x (x-t)^{-ν-1} z(t) dt + Σ_{n=1}^{∞} K_n x^{-n-ν}/Γ(1-n-ν),
where the K_n are arbitrary constants. This is the Riemann–Liouville fractional integral of order -ν with base point k, plus a 'complementary function'. The index shift (n_old+1 = n_new) matches exactly the series produced on the previous page by changing k.

(c) Footnote: all such arbitrary functions Σ K_n x^{-n-ν}/Π(-n-ν) are denoted C_ν. For positive integer n, every C_ν is also a C_{ν-n}.
Reason (verified by me): C_{ν-n} contains the exponents -ν+n-1, …, -ν, -ν-1, -ν-2, …. These include all exponents -ν-1, -ν-2, … of C_ν, with the same Γ-normalisation. Take the extra coefficients to be 0.

(d) Definition for ν > 0: ∂_x^ν z is the value obtained from ∂_x^{ν-m} z (m an integer, m > ν) by m-fold differentiation in x, i.e. ∂_x^ν z = d^m/dx^m ∂_x^{ν-m} z.
Implicit (mine): this is independent of m, since d/dx of the order-α fractional integral equals the order-(α-1) integral. Also d/dx [x^{s}/Π(s)] = x^{s-1}/Π(s-1), so complementary functions map to complementary functions: d^m C_{ν-m} is a C_ν. In modern terms this is the Riemann–Liouville derivative.

The sentence continues onto the next page: this value always satisfies the generalized Taylor equation (2), z(x+h) = Σ h^{ν+n}/Π(ν+n) ∂^{ν+n} z.
errors: No real error on this page.

Inherited from the previous page: the binomial/series expansion Σ x^{-μ-1-n}(-t)^n… used to justify the complementary series converges only when |t| < |x| for t between k1 and k. Without that restriction, the claim that changing k merely adds a C_ν is unjustified as stated.
Arbitrariness (not an error but a weakness): the complementary function with arbitrary K_n makes ∂^ν multivalued and non-unique. This was later criticized (e.g. Cayley 1880).

When ν is an integer, some Π(-n-ν) are infinite and the corresponding terms vanish. Riemann does not comment on this, though it is consistent with eq. 3 on the next page (finite polynomial complementary part).

results.what: Definition of the fractional integral of order -ν: (1/Γ(-ν)) ∫_k^x (x-t)^{-ν-1} z(t) dt
results.usually_credited_to: Liouville (1832ff.) / Riemann (1847, publ. 1876); the integral form goes back to Abel (1823)

results.what: Addition of the 'complementary function' Σ K_n x^{-n-ν}/Γ(1-n-ν), arising from the arbitrariness of the base point k
results.modern_name: Riemann's complementary function in fractional calculus

results.what: Fractional derivative for ν>0 defined as d^m/dx^m of the fractional integral of order m-ν
Nesting of complementary function classes: C_ν ⊂ C_{ν-n} for positive integer n
results.modern_name: elementary property of the complementary function

deep.surprise_reason: This page is part of Riemann's well-known 1847 essay on fractional integration/differentiation, printed in his Gesammelte Werke. The Riemann–Liouville integral and the complementary function are standardly credited to him from this very text.

d/dx [x^s/Π(s)] = x^{s-1}/Π(s-1), so differentiating a complementary function C_{ν-m} m times gives a C_ν.

transcription_corrections: Riemann writes ^x∂^ν_z (crossed out in the image) and the editor writes ∂_x^ν z in red. The transcription silently uses the editor's form.
In the summation the limits are written with n=1 above and n=∞ below, i.e. the sum runs over n = 1, 2, 3, …; this matches the transcription's Σ_{n=∞}^{n=1}.
Margin '**) p. 26. (1. 8. 26)' refers to the footnote placed on p. 26. The red '*) ∂_x^ν z 1.' is an editorial notation instruction, not mathematics.
The second red margin item 'Als Note unter den Text' marks the bracketed passage about C_ν (boxed in red) as a footnote.
In the margin the editor's replacement reads approximately ∂_x^{-m} ∂_x^{ν-m} z, but the text itself reads 'aus ∂_x^{ν-m} z (wo m>ν) durch m maliges Differentiiren'.
